input: CPU scheduling decides which ready process runs next. First-Come First-Served (FCFS) runs processes in arrival order and is simple but can cause the convoy effect, where short processes wait behind a long one. Shortest Job First (SJF) picks the process with the smallest next CPU burst and gives the minimum average waiting time, but it needs to know burst lengths in advance and can starve long processes. Round Robin (RR) gives each process a fixed time quantum in turn; if the quantum is too large RR behaves like FCFS, and if it is too small context-switch overhead increases.

input: Normalization reduces redundancy and update anomalies in relational schemas. A table is in First Normal Form (1NF) if all attributes hold atomic values and there are no repeating groups. A table is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and no non-key attribute depends transitively on the primary key.
